question: Does the mint-a-department baseline agreement lock a fixed, sealed test (metric, baseline, minimum improvement, direction, sample size, critical value) that both parties sign BEFORE any work, judge the delivery against that signed test alone so the goalpost cannot move, waive the charge whenever the delivery does not beat the signed baseline, keep the whole decision a re-runnable receipt, and never let a price touch the decision?
why: Simon's BUILD-TOMORROW plan (2026-11-01) PRIORITY 3: make mint-a-department sellable. 3a an intake (job, data, current tool/process, the baseline); 3b a baseline-agreement template — fixed test set + metric + minimum improvement, signed before work; 3c money-back terms, 'beats your signed baseline or you don't pay' (Simon sets the price — a DECISION). The guarantee is only safe because the test is sealed, pre-signed and independently re-runnable. This kernel is that agreement: it REUSES the gated-experiment engine (src/experiment.mjs, sealed 0b341b0) — the baseline agreement IS a sealed test, and 'beats the baseline' IS verdict(agreement.test, delivery) === PROMOTE. The flywheel: the growth team's gate is also the sales guarantee's gate.

design.where: A kernel in ai-first-company, src/baseline.mjs, reusing src/experiment.mjs. Pure, total, deterministic, witness-gated with zero survivors, nothing baselined. It carries no price in the decision and no client PII beyond the names the two parties put in their own agreement; it fetches nothing and signs nothing itself (Ed25519 signing is the parties', as in feed.mjs).
design.intake: What the client brings: { job, data, currentTool, client, supplier, metric, kind: 'rate'|'mean', baseline (their current measured level), direction: 'higher'|'lower' }. job/data/currentTool are plain description; metric..direction seed the sealed test.
design.design2: What the agreement adds (Simon/Delivery, written before work): { minImprovement (the smallest gain that counts as a win), minSample (per arm), zCrit (the critical value for the agreed confidence), price? (a placeholder the kernel never reads for the decision) }.
design.agreement: agreement(intake, design) → { ok, agreement } | { ok:false, why }. It builds the experiment sealedTest from intake+design (id from the job, channel = client:<client>, technique = delivery:<job>, metric/kind/baseline/direction/minImprovement/minSample/alpha/zCrit) and validates it with normalizeTest; an incomplete or malformed intake/design is refused with a reason. The agreement = { test, parties: {client, supplier}, moneyBack: 'beats the signed baseline or no charge', price }.
design.signable: signable(agreement) → the canonical bytes both parties sign BEFORE work: the fixed test, the parties, the money-back clause and the price — but NEVER any delivery result. Signing commits to the baseline before a result exists.
design.outcome: outcome(agreement, delivery) → { ok, beatsBaseline, decision, charge: 'due'|'waived', receipt, why }. The delivery is the measured result of the built system (the same {control, variant} arms the experiment gate reads). The verdict is verdict(agreement.test, delivery) — judged ONLY against the agreement's sealed test, never against anything in the delivery. beatsBaseline = decision === PROMOTE; charge = beatsBaseline ? 'due' : 'waived'. receipt = the SHA-256 of canonical(agreement.test, delivery-measurement, verdict) — no price, no proposer.

claims.claim: Agreement integrity: a complete intake+design yields an agreement whose test passes normalizeTest and whose signable bytes contain the test, parties, money-back clause and price but NO delivery; each of a battery of incomplete or malformed intakes/designs (missing job/metric/baseline/direction, a bad kind, a non-positive minImprovement, a sub-2 minSample, a non-positive zCrit) is refused with a reason.
claims.pass: all complete accepted; all malformed refused with a reason; signable carries no delivery

claims.claim: The goalpost cannot move: for every delivery, outcome() applies the AGREEMENT's sealed test only — injecting a different metric/baseline/target INTO the delivery object leaves beatsBaseline, charge and the receipt unchanged; and the same delivery arms judged under two agreements with different sealed tests give each agreement's own verdict.
claims.pass: 0 cases where a delivery-side field moves the outcome; two agreements differ as their tests do

claims.claim: Money-back is exact: over a 300-case battery of (agreement, delivery) pairs, charge is 'due' for exactly the deliveries that beat the signed baseline (verdict PROMOTE) and 'waived' for every DROP and INSUFFICIENT; no waived delivery is ever charged.
claims.pass: due count == PROMOTE count; every non-PROMOTE waived; 0 charged-but-not-beaten

claims.claim: Re-runnable receipt: every outcome's receipt is the SHA-256 of canonical(agreement.test, delivery-measurement, verdict) and re-derives from them; it is identical whoever delivered and whatever price the agreement carries.
claims.pass: all receipts re-derive; price- and proposer-independent

claims.claim: Total and deterministic: 3,000 fuzzed inputs (wrong types, missing fields, NaN/Infinity, malformed intakes, deliveries and agreements) raise nothing — each refused with a reason or a well-formed outcome; the same inputs give the same outcome and receipt every time.
claims.pass: 0 throws; all handled; byte-identical on repeat

claims.claim: Price never touches the decision: for every case, setting the agreement's price to any value, zero, or removing it leaves beatsBaseline, charge, decision and the receipt identical. The kernel sets no price and reads none for the verdict.
claims.pass: outcome and receipt unchanged across every price

notProven: This seals the AGREEMENT's logic — that a sealed, pre-signed baseline is judged honestly and the charge is waived when it is not beaten — not the price (Simon's, a decision), not the Stripe/payment flow (Simon connects it), not that any particular delivery will beat a given baseline (that is the delivery's own measured result), and not the teacher-distillation engine itself (fallforgemint/fallnode, already built and gated elsewhere). Signing is the parties' (Ed25519, as in feed.mjs); this kernel decides and signs nothing.
